sources_considered.why: Contemporaneous company announcement identifies an AI-designed candidate entering an efficacy-testing stage.
Primary disclosure distinguishes unsuccessful overall efficacy endpoints from exploratory subgroup findings.
An account coauthored by participants in the AI identification work documents the important repurposing distinction.
Although the tool labeled it FULL TEXT, the returned content explicitly says it is a subscription preview.
Potentially useful retrospective pipeline analysis, but read_page returned HTTP 403; its later aggregate reporting period also needs separation from the post-date cutoff.

evidence_items.explanation: The announcement describes these results as safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics in healthy participants, followed by entry into Phase II efficacy testing. It supports candidate status for this molecule, but cannot establish the absence of successful drugs elsewhere.

The company reported that BEN-2293 failed its overall efficacy endpoints. It also reported a subgroup signal requiring further investigation, which is weaker than established efficacy and prevents treating this as an absence of all biological activity.

The authors describe AI-assisted identification of baricitinib for COVID-19 and clinical benefit. This is material counterevidence to a broader reading covering all AI-assisted drug discovery, but the molecule was an existing treatment rather than newly designed by AI.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved candidate-specific records do not provide a comprehensive census sufficient to establish the universal negative.
The scope of AI involvement and the threshold for proven efficacy remain consequential ambiguities.
A readable, candidate-level account of successful efficacy trials before 2023-10-10 was not obtained.
